scope: One disposable Kind v1.36.1 cluster. Inert candidates carry equally verified provenance handoff records and separately supplied fictional trust evidence. A restricted Job persists disposition, rationale and reviewer data in Kubernetes. An admission policy using that record allows the assessed artifact digest and rejects the discrepant one. A supplemental native OIDC identity writes a separate digest-bound review disposition through a narrowly authorized Kubernetes API path, and a second admission policy reads that record for a distinct Pod label. This establishes fixture authentication, RBAC, record binding and gate behavior only. Real human authority, substantive review quality, publisher/community signals, independent provenance and production coverage remain adopter evidence.

checks.claim: Both provenance-complete model declarations pass before trust eligibility is required
The persisted review treats matching-quality provenance differently according to explicit trust evidence
The default workload identity cannot update the trust decision record
The same unapproved candidate is denied by Kubernetes admission
The approved candidate remains eligible under the same policy
An authenticated OIDC identity outside the reviewer group cannot write a disposition
The native OIDC reviewer writes and reads back a disposition bound to the exact candidate digest
The active review policy admits only the digest approved by the authenticated reviewer
